## SHOULD-FIX (accepted reviewer improvements; apply all)

### S1 — Pin the reproduction comparison to the base-commit corpus. (Statistics critic; the single most valuable non-blocking finding.)

A17's "~1-2 plan versions/day" is a two-point delta with an unstated
denominator, and it is wrong by roughly 20x. Measured off dated commits, net
corpus growth is **+23/day (1d), +24/day (3d), +35.6/day (7d), +40/day (14d)**.
New *mask-changing* arrivals are milder but bursty: 1 in the last 3 days, 1 in
the last 7, **14 in the last 14** (~1.0/day on the 14-day mean).

So ±3 covers about a **three-day** window, not the "same-week implementation"
§8 claims. On a long round S1 lands at 156-167, K2 fires, and K2's own escape
clause ("with no corpus-drift explanation") absorbs it — at which point S1/K2
can no longer do the one job they exist for: discriminating implementation
divergence from corpus drift.

**Fix (restores exact discrimination):** run the reproduction comparison against
the corpus **as of the base commit**:

```
git ls-tree -r <base-sha> | grep -E '^tasks/[^/]+/[^/]+/plans/v[0-9]+\.md$'
```

On that pinned set the answer must be **exactly 153 / 37 / 36 with NO
tolerance**. Report live-corpus arrivals as a separate line. Drift is monotone
(status changes are `git mv`; files are never removed), so a count **below** 153
on the pinned set is unambiguously a divergence. Keep the ± tolerances only for
the live-corpus line. Update A17, §6 S1-S3, §7 K2, and the §8 drift row.

### S2 — Record the audit run's git SHA; production-kind histograms are tree-dependent.

The production-kind mover set is dominated by checks that read the live repo
tree — c41 x7, c51 x6, c34 x6, c31 x4, c37 x3, plus c42 x2 and c46 x1, i.e.
**29 of 63 rows**. Two consequences to absorb in the plan:

- A repo mutation landing between pass 1 and pass 2 of the same file can produce
  a spurious mover row. Self-catching (§4.3's `explain` would show no mask-diff
  explanation), but say so.
- The transition DIRECTION for these checks is tree-dependent, and the
  implementer's worktree will contain this task's own new test files and
  modified `verify_plan.py`. So the production-kind per-check histogram is **not
  expected to reproduce plan-time exactly** even with a byte-correct
  implementation, while the file COUNT (36) is robust. Say this in §6 so a
  mismatch is not misread as divergence.

Record the audit run's git SHA alongside the corpus size and date in §10 and in
the adjudication doc.

### S3 — Add a per-file unclosed-at-EOF boolean to the AC2 JSON row schema.

AC2(c) promises a per-file unclosed flag, but §4.2's harness surface exposes
`unclosed_census(paths)` as a COUNT function and `explain(path)` as a per-file
classifier, while AC2(a)'s JSON row schema is
`(file, check id, old status, new status)` with no unclosed column. Since **19
of the 37** forced-kind movers are unclosed-driven, that flag is the single most
informative per-row covariate for the adjudication. Add one boolean column (or
a per-file section) to the JSON.

### S4 — Lead the adjudication doc with the PRODUCTION numbers. (Methodology critic.)

AC2's deliverable table currently leads with the forced-kind 37/19 set. A later
reader skimming it could carry "37 plans re-verdicted" forward as the fleet
impact, when the operative result is **36 files / 15 checks / ZERO overall
verdict flips**. Lead the adjudication doc's summary with the production
numbers; label the forced-kind set explicitly as the body-reproduction arm.
(Keep AC2's enumeration itself as the forced-kind superset — that decision is
endorsed.)

### S5 — Mark each class-A adjudication as substantive vs parse-mechanical. (Methodology critic.)

Roughly 33 of the forced-set file-check pairs are PASS→SKIP or SKIP→PASS, where
§4.3's single question reduces to "are the trigger words inside a code block?" —
answerable by inspection and class A by construction. The same holds for the 19
unclosed-at-EOF files, where the honest answer certifies the PARSE, not that the
check should be blind to what the author intended as prose.

Add a per-check field recording whether the class-A verdict is a **substantive**
read (the c31/#1176 shape, where the WARN was hand-confirmed correct) or a
**parse-mechanical** one, so a uniform wall of 25 "class A" verdicts is not read
as 25 independent substantive confirmations.

### S6 — Add the container-scope caveat to the `_fence_scan` docstring. (Methodology critic.)

The docstring's "exactly one deliberate deviation" is understated. A line-local
mask cannot implement CommonMark's **container scope**: a fence opened inside a
list item and never closed inside it ends at the container boundary in a real
parser but runs to EOF here. This is inherent to the primitive being replaced,
shared with #2384's reference implementation, and in the same direction as the
already-disclosed unclosed-fence hazard (the 19 unclosed-at-EOF files are its
empirical surface). Add one sentence next to the indentation deviation so the
next reader does not read "one deviation" as stronger than it is.
